questions.corrige_markdown:
**Photosynthesis** is the process by which green plants (and algae) containing chlorophyll make carbohydrates (glucose) from carbon dioxide and water, using light energy, and release oxygen.

$$6\,\mathrm{CO_2} + 6\,\mathrm{H_2O} \xrightarrow{\text{light, chlorophyll}} \mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6} + 6\,\mathrm{O_2}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: How is a green leaf adapted to carry out photosynthesis? *(7 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any seven of the following:

1. The leaf is **broad and flat**, with a large surface area to absorb a lot of light and carbon dioxide.
2. The leaf is **thin**, so that light reaches all the cells and gases diffuse over a short distance.
3. The **upper epidermis is transparent** and has a thin cuticle, so light passes through to the mesophyll.
4. The **palisade cells** are tall, closely packed under the upper epidermis and contain **many chloroplasts**, so they absorb most of the light.
5. The **spongy mesophyll** has large air spaces, so that carbon dioxide diffuses easily to the cells and oxygen diffuses out.
6. The **stomata**, mostly in the lower epidermis, let carbon dioxide in and oxygen out; the **guard cells** control their opening.
7. The **xylem** of the veins brings water and mineral salts to the cells, and the **phloem** carries away the sugar made.
8. The **waxy cuticle** reduces water loss.
9. The leaves are arranged in a **leaf mosaic** and are held by the petiole towards the light, so that they do not shade one another.

questions.enonce_markdown: With the aid of an illustrated diagram only, show how water circulates in an ecosystem. *(7 marks)*
State the role played by producers in an ecosystem. *(3 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any three of the following:

1. Producers (green plants and algae) **trap light energy** and change it into chemical energy in food by photosynthesis.
2. They are the **first trophic level**: they make the food on which all the consumers depend, directly or indirectly.
3. They **release oxygen** into the air and use up carbon dioxide, which keeps the composition of the atmosphere constant.
4. They provide **shelter and habitats** for animals.
